content: The Global Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) guidance, now in its second edition, serves as a comprehensive framework to support countries in implementing strategies to improve adolescent health and well-being. Published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2023, this document builds on the first edition released in 2017, incorporating lessons learned, updated data, and new insights from the COVID-19 pandemic. It emphasizes the importance of investing in adolescent health as a means to achieve a triple dividend of benefits: improving the current health of adolescents, enhancing their future adult lives, and positively impacting the next generation. The guidance integrates the latest evidence on adolescent health, mortality, morbidity, and well-being determinants. It also highlights the consensus on core indicators for monitoring adolescent health and well-being. Furthermore, it incorporates the Adolescent Well-Being Framework, developed in collaboration with the Partnership for Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (PMNCH) and UN agencies, to guide programming efforts. The document underscores the need for multisectoral action, youth engagement, and evidence-based interventions to address the diverse needs of adolescents, particularly in fragile and humanitarian settings. The second edition also reflects significant political and scientific advancements since 2017. It advocates for a holistic approach to adolescent health, recognizing the interconnectedness of health, education, nutrition, and life skills. The guidance aligns with global initiatives such as the Education Plus program, which aims to empower girls by ensuring secondary education completion, access to youth-friendly health services, and economic opportunities, thereby reducing HIV risks and promoting gender equality. WHO emphasizes the importance of creating safe, respectful, and empowering environments for adolescents. The establishment of the WHO Youth Council exemplifies efforts to amplify young people's voices and leverage their expertise in shaping public health policies. The guidance also calls for strengthened partnerships among global stakeholders to advance adolescent health and well-being, ensuring equitable access to essential services and addressing inequalities. The document acknowledges the critical role of education in promoting health and well-being, as highlighted by UNESCO. It advocates for integrating health and education systems to create environments where adolescents can thrive. Similarly, UNFPA and UNICEF stress the importance of sexual and reproductive health programs, social service systems, and community engagement to support adolescents' transition into adulthood. The guidance also highlights the role of nutrition, as emphasized by the World Food Programme (WFP), in addressing the unique needs of adolescents, particularly in vulnerable settings. It calls for increased access to affordable, nutritious diets to combat malnutrition and support adolescents' development. Overall, the second edition of the AA-HA. guidance provides a roadmap for countries to adopt evidence-informed, multisectoral approaches to adolescent health.
